title: Behavioral Economics And Energy Consumption
titleZh: 行为经济学与能源消耗

parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Part four. You will hear a lecture about behavioral economics and energy use. First, you have some time to look at questions thirty-one to forty.

Now listen carefully and answer questions thirty-one to forty.

Good morning, everyone. Today, we're looking at how behavioral economics can help explain the way people use energy at home. This is useful because many governments and energy companies want households to reduce consumption, but simply giving people information does not always work. Traditional economists often imagine consumers as careful decision-makers. In this view, people compare costs and benefits, think through the available evidence, and choose rationally, as if every decision were based on logic. Behavioral economics takes a different view. It suggests that many everyday choices are made quickly and almost automatically. Instead of analyzing every detail, people are often guided by habit, emotion, or instinct. A simple example comes from a savings program. Participants were attracted by the chance of winning a prize, even though the mathematical probability was very low. What mattered to them was the possibility of gaining something, not the actual likelihood of success.

Now let's turn to an energy project involving household customers. Researchers expected that giving people advice would make them use less energy. But in some cases, the figures moved in the opposite direction and showed an increase. This was surprising because the scheme had been designed to reduce consumption. The customers were divided into four groups. Each group received a different message about why they should cut down on energy use. One message focused on saving money. Another emphasized environmental protection. A third said that using less energy would help people living nearby, especially their neighbors. The final group was told that many other households in the local area were already using less energy. Only this group actually changed its behavior. So what can be done to encourage change? One lesson is that facts alone are often not enough. People may respond better when there is some form of reward, even a small one, such as a discount or positive feedback.

Another useful tool is technology. Smart meters, phone apps, and reminders can make energy use easier to notice. It is also important to remember that progress does not always require major action. Small changes in routine can still produce useful results, such as reducing heating or switching off unused lights. There is also a role for the government, especially in funding schemes that help households improve energy efficiency. For example, a family may use much less energy if an old heating system is replaced with a modern boiler.

That is the end of part four. You now have forty-five seconds to check your answers to part four.

analyses.content: 录音里提到的“choose rationally”对应了题目里的“act rationally”，意思就是凭逻辑理性地做决定。
你可能会听到上一句很清晰的“decision-makers”，但要注意题目空格前是动词“act”，需要填一个副词，所以只能填“rationally”。

Traditional economists often imagine consumers as careful decision-makers. In this view, people compare costs and benefits, think through the available evidence, and choose rationally, as if every decision were based on logic.
录音中的“guided by... instinct”直接表明被本能引导，完美替换了题目里的“rely on instinct”。
录音并列给出了“habit, emotion, or instinct”三个词，只需要填入题干缺少的 instinct 即可。

Behavioral economics takes a different view. It suggests that many everyday choices are made quickly and almost automatically. Instead of analyzing every detail, people are often guided by habit, emotion, or instinct.
题目意思是“看重获得的可能而不是成功的...”，刚好对应录音最后对比部分指出的“not the actual likelihood of success”。
前面提到了一个意思相近的干扰词“probability”，但它修饰的是获奖几率，而只有“likelihood”紧跟着题目要求的“of success”。

A simple example comes from a savings program. Participants were attracted by the chance of winning a prize, even though the mathematical probability was very low. What mattered to them was the possibility of gaining something, not the actual likelihood of success.
题目说导致了一个出乎意料的结果，录音里的“showed an increase”对应结果，紧接着的“surprising”刚好替换了“unexpected”。
你可能会听到“opposite direction”并试图自己去拼凑答案，但填空题只能填录音里实实在在读出来的那个明确结果“increase”。

Researchers expected that giving people advice would make them use less energy. But in some cases, the figures moved in the opposite direction and showed an increase. This was surprising because the scheme had been designed to reduce consumption.
录音中的动词“help”直接同义替换了题目里的“benefits to（对...有好处）”，明确指出了对象是他们的“neighbors”。
刚听到“people”时你可能就想填了，但录音紧跟着用“especially”强调了更具体精准的受众群，所以答案必须是“neighbors”。
A third said that using less energy would help people living nearby, especially their neighbors.
题目问人们想要什么，录音说人们在有某种“reward”的时候反应更好，直接对应了题目想要表达的诉求。
录音马上跟了具体的例子“discount”或“feedback”，你可能很容易被细节干扰，错过了前面起统领作用的核心词“reward”。

So what can be done to encourage change? One lesson is that facts alone are often not enough. People may respond better when there is some form of reward, even a small one, such as a discount or positive feedback.
录音直接用“Another useful tool”引出新方法，“tool”在这里就是“way”的替换，直接锁定核心词“technology”。
紧接着录音举例了“Smart meters”和“phone apps”，你可能顺手填了这些具体的应用词，而忽略了这一整段的大方向总起词。
Another useful tool is technology. Smart meters, phone apps, and reminders can make energy use easier to notice.
录音里的“Small”替换了题目的“minor”，所以直接填后面的名词“changes”，而“produce useful results”就是“have an effect”的同义表达。
你可能觉得“changes”这个词太简单不敢写，或者被后面的“routine”拐跑了，切记直接紧跟形容词替换词的往往就是答案。

It is also important to remember that progress does not always require major action. Small changes in routine can still produce useful results, such as reducing heating or switching off unused lights.
题目问谁应该在这方面花钱，录音里提到了“funding（出资）”这个动作，而执行这个动作的角色是“government”。
如果你反应不过来“funding”就是“spend money”的替换，可能就会漏听这句，导致无法将主语“government”抓准。
There is also a role for the government, especially in funding schemes that help households improve energy efficiency.
录音中的“replaced with（替换为）”完美匹配了题干里的动词“change a”，换上的新设备就是“boiler”。
你可能会听到前面的“heating system”，但那是原本就被淘汰的旧东西，题目需要你填的是更新后的物件，所以必须是“boiler”。
For example, a family may use much less energy if an old heating system is replaced with a modern boiler.
